```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette walks through the Two-Stage TMLE pipeline of Balzer *et al.*
(2021) on simulated cluster randomized trial (CRT) data. We will:

1. Generate one simulated CRT (30 clusters, 100-200 participants per cluster,
   pair-matched, post-baseline missingness).
2. Run **Stage 1** — within each cluster, an individual-level TMLE that
   adjusts for differential outcome measurement.
3. Run **Stage 2** — a cluster-level TMLE with Adaptive Pre-specification
   that picks the adjustment variable that maximises empirical efficiency.
4. Inspect point estimates, 95% confidence intervals, and the IC-based
   variance.

The simulation data-generating process is the same one used in the paper
(§ 5). It is bundled inside the package for testing and reproducibility but
is not exported — you can access it via `TwoStageTMLE:::gen_data_complex()`.

## Generate a single trial

```{r generate}
library(TwoStageTMLE)
library(data.table)

set.seed(1)
J <- 30
n <- c(100, 150, 200)
X_all <- TwoStageTMLE:::gen_data_complex(effect = TRUE, n = n, J = J)
head(X_all)
```

Each row is an individual; `id` is the cluster, `pair` is the matched-pair
identifier, `A` is the cluster-level treatment, `Delta` indicates whether
the outcome was measured, `Y` is the (possibly missing) outcome, and
`Y.1` / `Y.0` are the counterfactual outcomes (known here because we
simulated them). `X1`, `X2`, `M` are individual covariates; `X1.c`, `X2.c`
are the cluster-level means of `X1`, `X2`.

Mask the missing outcomes and drop the counterfactuals — that's what a real
analyst would see:

```{r mask}
O <- TwoStageTMLE:::get_obs(X_all, exclude = FALSE)
head(O[, c("id", "pair", "A", "X1", "X2", "M", "Delta", "Y")])
```

## Stage 1: cluster-specific endpoints

Stage 1 estimates the cluster-specific mean outcome `Y^c` controlling for
differential measurement. Within each cluster separately, we fit an
individual-level TMLE with `Delta` as the "treatment" node (we are
hypothetically intervening to set `Delta = 1`) and adjustment variables
`W = (X1, X2, M)`.

`stage1_tmle()` is an **internal reference implementation** of the Balzer et al.
(2021) Stage 1 (hence the `TwoStageTMLE:::` prefix); the package's public API is
the general building blocks ([stage1_mean()], [stage1_apply()], [stage2_tmle()]),
and this vignette documents how the paper method composes from them.

```{r stage1}
stage1 <- TwoStageTMLE:::stage1_tmle(
  data = O,
  ind_cov = c("X1", "X2", "M"),
  clust_cov = c("X1.c", "X2.c"),
  sl_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.gam")
)
stage1
```

Each row is one cluster. `unadj` is the simple mean of measured outcomes
(unadjusted Stage 1 estimator) and `tmle` is the TMLE estimate of `Y^c`.
The two columns should differ when missingness depends on the covariates.

## Stage 2: intervention effect with Adaptive Pre-specification

Stage 2 takes those cluster-specific endpoints and fits a cluster-level
TMLE comparing intervention to control. Adaptive Pre-specification picks
the single adjustment variable that minimises the cross-validated variance
of the resulting estimator. For this trial we let APS choose from `X1.c`,
`X2.c`, or no adjustment (`U`).

```{r stage2}
stage2_in <- copy(stage1)
stage2_in[, Y := tmle]              # use the Stage 1 TMLE as outcome
stage2_in <- add_weights(stage2_in, target = "clust")

cand <- cand_adj(c("X1.c", "X2.c"))

est <- stage2_tmle(
  data = stage2_in,
  goal = "RD",
  target = "clust",
  break_match = FALSE,              # preserve the matched pairs
  do_data_adapt = TRUE,
  cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
  cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form
)
est[, .(est, ci_lo, ci_hi, se, pval, q_adj, g_adj)]
```

Key columns in the output:

* `est` — point estimate of the risk difference (back-transformed to the
  natural scale).
* `ci_lo`, `ci_hi` — 95% confidence interval.
* `se` — IC-based standard error on the log scale for `aRR` / `OR`,
  natural scale for `RD`.
* `pval` — two-sided p-value (use `one_sided = TRUE` and `alt_smaller` to
  test a one-sided alternative).
* `q_adj`, `g_adj` — index into `cand_q_adj` / `cand_g_adj` of the
  variable APS chose (1 = the unadjusted estimator `"U"`).

## End-to-end driver

The two-step procedure above can be run as a single call:

```{r e2e, eval = FALSE}
out <- TwoStageTMLE:::two_stage_tmle(
  data = O,
  ind_cov = c("X1", "X2", "M"),
  clust_cov = c("X1.c", "X2.c"),
  goal = "RD", target = "clust", break_match = FALSE,
  do_data_adapt = TRUE,
  cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
  cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form
)
out$est        # Stage 2 estimate
out$stage1     # cluster-level data with `unadj` and `tmle` columns
```

## When to use what

* `goal`: `"RD"` for risk difference, `"aRR"` for arithmetic risk ratio,
  `"OR"` for odds ratio. The paper focuses on `RD` and `aRR`; `OR` is
  supported but not validated against published results.
* `target`: `"clust"` if you want the cluster-level effect (each cluster
  weighted equally), `"indv"` if you want the individual-level effect
  (each participant weighted equally). The two coincide when cluster
  sizes are equal.
* `break_match`: in pair-matched designs, `FALSE` preserves the matches
  (variance estimated over `N/2` pair sums; `t` with `N/2 - 1` df) and
  `TRUE` treats clusters as independent (variance over `N` clusters;
  `t` with `N - 2` df). The paper recommends preserving the matches when
  pair-matching was used for randomisation; doing so typically yields
  more power.
* `do_data_adapt`: `TRUE` runs Adaptive Pre-specification. `FALSE` uses
  the `q_adj` / `g_adj` you pass in directly (or the unadjusted estimator
  if both are `NULL`).
* `remove_pscore`: see the package's `questions_for_laura.md`; this
  argument controls whether the variable APS picks for `q_adj` is
  excluded from the `g_adj` candidate set. In a CRT with few clusters
  and only main-terms GLMs as candidates, `TRUE` matches the original
  2021 paper behaviour.

## References

Balzer L.B., van der Laan M., Ayieko J., Kamya M., Chamie G., Schwab J.,
Havlir D., Petersen M. (2021).
**Two-Stage TMLE to Reduce Bias and Improve Efficiency in Cluster
Randomized Trials.**
<https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15737>

Balzer L.B., van der Laan M., Petersen M., SEARCH Consortium (2016).
**Adaptive pre-specification in randomized trials with and without
pair-matching.**
*Statistics in Medicine* 35(10):4528-4545.
